translation.text: In those days chosen and holy children[a] will descend from high heaven, and their offspring will become one with humankind.

footnotes.text: The printed Ge’ez retains the word “children.” The compressed wording may also be understood as “children of the chosen and holy ones.” Charles brackets the passage from 38:6 through the first part of 39:2 as an interpolation; it is retained here with that editorial judgment disclosed.

translation.text: In those days Enoch received books of zeal and wrath, and books of tumult and confusion.[a] “Mercy will not be upon them,” says the Lord of Spirits.

translation.text: In that place my eyes saw the Chosen One of righteousness and faithfulness.[a] Righteousness will be in his days, and the righteous and chosen will be without number before him forever and ever.

footnotes.text: Charles prints the singular “Chosen One.” His apparatus records plural readings and readings with an added word for “dwelling place.” This translation follows the selected critical text, not unanimous manuscript testimony. “Faithfulness” may also be rendered “faith.”

independent_review_targets: Confirm first glyph of ኅሩየ and plural ኅሩያን.

translation.text: I saw a dwelling place beneath the wings of the Lord of Spirits. All the righteous and chosen shine[a] before him like the light of fire. Their mouth is filled with blessing, and their lips praise the name of the Lord of Spirits. Righteousness never comes to an end before him, and uprightness never comes to an end before him.[b]

footnotes.text: The verb in this comparison has divergent manuscript readings; “shine” follows the printed line’s comparison with the light of fire. The exact verbal reading requires independent scan review.
The final uprightness clause is printed by Charles, but the apparatus records its omission in several manuscripts.

independent_review_targets: Verify source verb ይትሰሐዩ, semantic force, and whether reader crux note should instead preserve non-finite/uncertain reading.
